title: DISCLOSURE_POLICY says crypto-erasure is available; no builtin performs it
claim: Section 3 lists crypto-erasure as available, but no builtin erases or re-wraps a record key; the only route is deleting key files by hand.
evidence: No erase/destroy builtin in builtin/record.go or builtin/case_key.go; the builtin registry has none.
fix_proposal: Stage E7: record_erase and case_key_erase, and rewrite sections 3 and 7 to state exactly what each destroys and what it cannot reach.

title: A Withdrawal records no authority
claim: DISCLOSURE_POLICY says a withdrawal records on whose authority it was made; the Withdrawal node gets only WITHDREW and PERFORMED_BY edges.
evidence: disclosureWriteWithdrawal writes no AUTHORISED_BY edge and no authority property.
fix_proposal: Stage E1: disclose_withdraw takes {authorised_by}; the Withdrawal gets an AUTHORISED_BY edge to the authority's Actor node and the role recorded.

title: The disclosure guard's file list omits two files that hold key material
claim: builtin/custody.go (caseKey, classTagKey) and case_key_passphrase.go are not in DisclosureFiles, so the no-plaintext-rendering guard does not look at them, and nothing detects an omission.
evidence: DisclosureFiles lists 13 files; neither is among them.
fix_proposal: Add both, and add TestEveryFileHoldingKeyMaterialIsGuarded so a file handling key material cannot be left off the list.

title: db_add_relation never persists its relation label
claim: The relation string goes only to an in-memory timeline that db_close clears; the stored edge is a plain DATA edge with no properties, while GRAPH_DATABASE.md says nodes are linked with a string relation label.
evidence: DbAddRelation (builtin/db_wrappers.go:72) calls AddEdge with no properties.
fix_proposal: Stage D2: one transaction adds the edge and indexes relation on it; db_relations reads it back; the CHANGELOG says labels on existing stores were never written.

title: The language server told editors it was version 0.1.0
claim: serverInfo.version was the constant 0.1.0, which no release of the language or the extension ever had, while mlsp --version printed global.Version.
evidence: serverVersion = "0.1.0"
repro: TestInitializeAdvertisesMVPCapabilities asserts ServerInfo.Version == global.Version and fails against the constant.
fix_proposal: serverVersion reads global.Version.

title: net_syn_scan is called deprecated but not marked deprecated
claim: The alias is documented as deprecated, but its metadata carries no StabilityDeprecated, so the editor's builtinDeprecated diagnostic never fires for it.
evidence: No builtin is marked StabilityDeprecated; the deprecated-builtin analyzer test self-skips.
fix_proposal: Mark it StabilityDeprecated with DeprecatedBy net_connect_scan and a stated removal version (3.0).

title: SECURITY.md named 2.4.x as the supported release
claim: The supported-versions table said 2.4.x was current a release after 2.5.0 shipped.
evidence: | 2.4.x | current |
repro: TestSecurityPolicySupportsThisMinor fails against the old table.
fix_proposal: The table names the current minor; the version test holds it to global.Version.

title: Example READMEs taught mutant run with -pwd
claim: Three READMEs taught the legacy run alias and the deprecated -pwd flag, which puts the password in the process table.
evidence: examples/project/portscan_service/README.md:42, examples/workshop/README.md:84, examples/workshop/RUN_SHEET_2H.md:41 and :71
repro: TestDocumentedCommandLinesExist fails on all three.
fix_proposal: Teach mutant gen --src and a prompt, --password-file or --password-stdin.

title: Four source comments cited a design note that does not exist
claim: dap/protocol.go, dap/session.go, generator/generate.go and vm/debugger.go cited plans/T1_DEBUGGER.md, which exists nowhere and would be gitignored if it did.
evidence: plans/ is in .gitignore; no such file exists locally either.
repro: TestCitedPathsExist fails on all four comments.
fix_proposal: Point them at the sections of docs/DEBUGGING.md that state the same decisions.

title: Analyzer comments state builtin counts three releases old
claim: Comments in hover_card.go, builtin_types.go, language_teach.go, builtin_pair_return.go, unchecked_error.go and webrepl/browser_safe.go quote 399, 409 or 459 builtins in the present tense; the registry holds 659.
evidence: git grep for the numbers in those files.
repro: git grep -n -E '\b(399|409|459)\b' lsp/internal/analyzer webrepl
fix_proposal: State the property instead of a count, or derive the count at runtime.

title: Two roadmap-era documents describe the tree as it was planned
claim: IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE says tests cover env combinations, which the configuration policy forbids; SECURITY_ENHANCEMENTS lists shipped items (--seed, sweep levels) as planned.
evidence: docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md:89, docs/SECURITY_ENHANCEMENTS.md:71-75 and :128-140
fix_proposal: Rewrite both against the tree, or archive them with a banner (owner's call at checkpoint B).

title: Anti-tamper probes route to a detail that says not implemented yet
claim: Unrouted probes report AntiTamperDetailNotImplemented, a probe result that describes an absence of implementation rather than a measurement.
evidence: security/antitamper_constants.go:22
fix_proposal: Implement each routed probe or remove it from routing; nothing reports a result it did not measure.

title: Bytecode is read with no size cap
claim: The artifact decode path reads its input with io.ReadAll and no bound, so an oversized or crafted artifact is loaded whole before anything checks it.
evidence: runner/runner.go:353
fix_proposal: Bound the read with a named limit and refuse beyond it.

title: 2.5.0 promised bare --password would be refused in the next minor
claim: The warning, main.go help, README.md:130 and CONFIGURATION_POLICY.md:174 all say --password will require --password-insecure in the next minor release; 2.6.0 is that release.
evidence: Promise added in 051045d, shipped in v2.5.0.
repro: mutant x.mu --password p warns and runs.
fix_proposal: Refuse bare --password, naming --password-insecure, --password-file and --password-stdin; reword the four texts as done.

title: A crash during sealing leaves a torn record under its final name
claim: recordWriteFile creates the final path with O_EXCL and removes it only on a reported error, so a killed process leaves a partial .mrec where a complete one is expected; key files already write to a temporary file, sync and rename.
evidence: builtin/record.go:764 and :776 against builtin/case_key.go:665
fix_proposal: Seal to a temporary file, fsync, rename; a crash-child test proves no torn record survives.

title: Type uses across modules never reach the symbol graph
claim: lookupType is file-local, so a struct literal or enum reference to a type declared in another module is recorded as unbound and gets no USES_TYPE edge, although the compiler resolves it.
evidence: sema/graph_walk.go:378 notes UnboundType; the compiler resolves across the program in compile order.
fix_proposal: Stage D5: resolve such uses at export in compile order and count what cannot be resolved.

title: db_bfs and db_shortest_path misread their arguments
claim: An unknown direction silently means both; parallel edges are lost; neither walk has a budget; db_shortest_path ignores direction and returns an error where its metadata says an empty result.
evidence: builtin/db.go:448, :490, :598-607; builtin/metadata.go:2199
fix_proposal: Stage D4: refuse a bad direction or negative depth, budget both walks, return every edge in the walked direction, correct the metadata.

title: Two ledger reads can be silently wrong
claim: ledger_query_nodes on a key that was never indexed returns an empty result with no error; ledger_path uses an undirected search and never says a hop ran against its edge.
evidence: builtin/ledger_read.go:611 and :1211-1249; graphene v0.9.0 dijkstra is undirected.
fix_proposal: Refuse or flag an unindexed key; mark each reversed hop.

title: The label table is rewritten and fsynced on every disclosure write
claim: DeclareTypeNames runs on every disclosure, withdrawal and reclassification write, and graphene rewrites graphene.labels unconditionally.
evidence: disclose_ledger.go:533, disclose_history.go:199, disclose_reclassify.go:264
fix_proposal: Declare the type names once per ledger session.

title: graph export drops the store's Close error
claim: An export that fails to close its store reports success.
evidence: cli/graph.go:271
fix_proposal: Return the Close error.

title: Unclosed graph handles live until the process exits
claim: A script that forgets db_close or ledger_close leaves the store open until exit, and the next open reports an unclean shutdown; the only sweep is test-only.
evidence: builtin/ledger.go:803
fix_proposal: Close open handles at program exit with a warning naming each.

title: db_add_node on an exported symbol store writes nodes the query side cannot decode
claim: graphene's label registry is process-global; custom type 0 is db_* DATA and also the symbol graph's Module, so db_open_disk on an exported store writes Module-labelled nodes that loadModules then fails to decode.
evidence: graphene typenames.go:136-156; cli/graph_query.go:619
fix_proposal: A policy test that no two graph families give one label number two names, and db_open_disk refuses a symbol store for writing.

title: db_* properties can be written and indexed but never read by key
claim: Scripts can index node properties but have no builtin to look a node up by one.
evidence: GRAPH_DATABASE.md:150-163 says so.
fix_proposal: Stage D3: db_find, db_node, db_relations, db_schema.

title: The CHANGELOG misdates 2.5.0 and files its entries under Unreleased
claim: [2.5.0] is dated 2026-09-14 but the tag was made 2026-09-17; thirteen [Unreleased] entries (Sigma, C-1, C-2, ED-3, ED-4, the CI removal and others) shipped in that tag; 14d4ea5 and a901ce4 have no entry; the deps entry says graphene v0.9.0 was already current when 2.5.0 shipped v0.4.0.
evidence: git log -1 --format=%ci v2.5.0; git merge-base --is-ancestor for each entry's commit.
repro: git merge-base --is-ancestor f5fd64c v2.5.0 exits 0 while the Sigma entry sits under [Unreleased].
fix_proposal: Move the entries, re-date 2.5.0 to 2026-09-17, add the missing entries, correct the graphene line; the release gate checks the heading date against the tag.
regression_test: scripts/release_gate step: CHANGELOG date matches the tag; cmd/gendocs TestChangelogLeadsWithThisVersion

title: A MODULES.md example used a comment syntax Mutant does not have
claim: The private-names example elided its bodies with /* ... */, which does not parse, so a reader pasting it got a syntax error.
evidence: parse: no prefix parse function for /
repro: TestDocumentedProgramsCompile fails on the fence.
fix_proposal: Give the example real bodies.

title: Two links into the capability reference pointed at anchors that no longer exist
claim: SECURE_NETWORKING linked #network-32 and TESTING linked #testing; the headings carry the current counts (#network-33, #testing-10).
evidence: docs/CAPABILITY_REFERENCE.md headings
repro: TestDocumentLinksResolve fails on both.
fix_proposal: Point at the current anchors; the link test catches the next drift.

title: CONTRIBUTING pointed at the packaging script's old location
claim: scripts/package-targets.mjs lives at mutant-vscode-extension/scripts/package-targets.mjs.
evidence: No scripts/package-targets.mjs exists.
repro: TestCitedPathsExist fails on the line.
fix_proposal: Cite the real path.

title: Four example programs were reachable from no README
claim: examples/README.md never named collections/, crypto/ or structured/, and the evidence README never named its own export_mft.mut; the old test only looked at top-level directories that had a README.
evidence: examples/collections/data_pipeline.mut, examples/crypto/crypto_toolkit.mut, examples/structured/json_config_pipeline.mut, examples/workshop/evidence/export_mft.mut
repro: TestEveryExampleIsListedInItsReadme, now recursive, fails on all four.
fix_proposal: List them; the test now walks every directory and checks the reverse.

title: The example sweep passes --password, which 2.6.0 will refuse
claim: compile, execute and startAndStop all pass --password; once bare --password is refused the whole sweep fails.
evidence: cmd/sweep/sweeper.go:115, :242 and :265
fix_proposal: Pass --password-insecure (the explicit opt-in) in the same change that refuses bare --password.

title: LuaPatch carried a field nothing set, which storage dropped anyway
claim: DecryptedChecksum was documented as set after decryption for validation, but no code set or read it, and mutil.EncryptObject/DecryptObject rebuilt LuaPatch without it, so it could not have survived a store in any case.
evidence: git grep DecryptedChecksum finds only the declaration; runtime/lua/lua.go:46 validates against ChecksumExpected.
repro: TestEveryObjectFieldSurvivesStorage fails: DecryptedChecksum stored, loaded empty.
fix_proposal: Remove the field; say where validation really happens.

title: Every read of a variable costs time in proportion to its size
claim: The VM keeps each variable encrypted and decrypts it on every load, so a loop that reads a large Bytes value pays for the whole value on each iteration. A script that walks a 3 MiB file with bytes_read_* takes about a minute.
evidence: examples/binary/static_bin_analysis.mut, which parses the 3 MiB examples/data/sample_win.exe, runs for 61.8 s at mutation 0 and fails the sweep's 60 s per-run limit. Two probes with the same 2000-iteration bytes_read_u32_le loop: over the whole 3 MiB file 47.2 s, over a 16 KiB slice of it 2.4 s (mostly start-up), about 23 ms per read at 3 MiB.
repro: let data, err = fs_read("examples/data/sample_win.exe"); then for i in 0..2000 { bytes_read_u32_le(data, i * 4) }; compare with data = bytes_slice(data, 0, 16384). Compile with mutant gen and run each; wall time scales with the buffer, not the loop.
impact: Forensic scripts read large buffers in loops as a matter of course; this makes them quadratic in practice. It also fails the release gate's example sweep.
fix_proposal: Stage B PERF to establish where the time goes (decrypt, copy, or both) and design a representation that does not re-process an unchanged value on every load, without weakening what variable encryption protects against. Stage G adds a benchmark over a large Bytes variable.

title: fs_hash on a directory reports the host's words for the error
claim: fs_hash opens a directory and reads it, so the refusal is whatever the OS says: "Incorrect function." on Windows and "is a directory" on Linux. A script cannot tell the cases apart portably, and a golden recorded on one host fails on the other.
evidence: Windows sweep at 07c737a: "read examples/data: Incorrect function."; WSL sweep at 07c737a, same program: "read examples/data: is a directory".
fix_proposal: Stat first and refuse a directory with the builtin's own message, the same on every OS. fs_integrity_baseline no longer hashes directories (M26-EX-003), so a builtin test has to hold this.
repro: fs_hash("examples/data") on Windows and on Linux; the two errors differ in their words.

title: binary_analysis_example analyses a file that is not there
claim: Every bin_* call is pointed at README.md, which is not in the tree the example runs from, so the example demonstrates eight error messages and no analysis.
evidence: examples/binary/binary_analysis_example.golden: every line is an error (open README.md: no such file or directory; unsupported or invalid binary format).
repro: go run ./cmd/sweep -v examples/binary/binary_analysis_example.mut
fix_proposal: Point it at examples/data/sample_win.exe (or a smaller fixture) and re-record the golden.

title: mini_timeline_builder indexes a null error field
claim: The example passes fs_stat's error field to db_index_prop unconditionally; for a file that stats cleanly the field is null and db_index_prop refuses it, so the output is a run of argument errors.
evidence: examples/graph/mini_timeline_builder.golden lines 4-6: argument 4 to `db_index_prop` must be STRING, got NULL.
repro: go run ./cmd/sweep -v examples/graph/mini_timeline_builder.mut
fix_proposal: Index the error only when it is a string, and re-record the golden.

title: fs_integrity_baseline hashes the directories fs_walk returns
claim: The loop calls fs_hash on every entry fs_walk returns, including the walk root, so its baseline starts with a hash error.
evidence: examples/filesystem/fs_integrity_baseline.golden line 4: hash error: examples/data.
repro: go run ./cmd/sweep -v examples/filesystem/fs_integrity_baseline.mut
fix_proposal: Skip directory entries and print each entry by name; see M26-BLT-002 for the builtin half.
regression_test: go run ./cmd/sweep --golden examples/filesystem/fs_integrity_baseline.mut (the golden records no hash error)

title: registry_persistence_hunt queries a Run key its fixture does not contain
claim: The hunt's central query, the HKCU Run key, is not in examples/data/offline_hive.json, so the example reports key not found where it means to show persistence.
evidence: examples/registry/registry_persistence_hunt.golden line 3.
repro: go run ./cmd/sweep -v examples/registry/registry_persistence_hunt.mut
fix_proposal: Add a Run key with one suspicious value to the fixture, or query a key it has.

title: The example sweep reached the internet and recorded host-specific output
claim: Thirty-three examples need something a sweep cannot supply (an evidence image the repository does not ship, a peer on the internet, a passphrase, or the machine they describe), yet the sweep ran them. Their goldens recorded a live certificate, localhost port states, and missing-file errors, so the release gate depended on the network and on the host.
evidence: The first --update-golden run wrote goldens holding example.com's TLS issuer and expiry, connectex errors for 127.0.0.1:22/80/8080, and nine 'cannot find the file' lines for disk images; command_sandbox recorded this machine's account name. The Linux baseline added security_environment_report, whose golden recorded this machine's sandbox verdict and risk score (false/VM/5 on Windows, true/WSL/100 under WSL).
repro: go run ./cmd/sweep --update-golden, then read the goldens.
fix_proposal: Mark the 33 with `// mutant:sweep needs-input -- <what>` and delete their goldens; command_sandbox prints that whoami ran, not what it printed.

title: Goldens recorded on Windows could not check a run on Linux
claim: A runtime error names its source position with the host's path separator, and Go words a missing file or a refused connection in the host's language, so every golden that recorded an honest error was Windows-only.
evidence: Eight of the goldens that remain held 'at examples\...' positions and 'The system cannot find the file specified.' or 'connectex: ...' text.
repro: Compare examples/binary/binary_analysis_example.golden with the same run on Linux.
fix_proposal: NormalizeOutput rewrites a runtime error's source position to forward slashes and maps the three Windows error texts to their POSIX words; --update-golden rewrites a golden whose stored bytes are not already in that form.

title: A failed task's error names the instruction pointer, which changes with the mutation level
claim: A VM runtime error carries 'vm_runtime_error ip=N op=...'. When a spawned task fails, task_wait hands that text to the script as a value, so a program that prints it prints different output at different mutation levels, which breaks the promise that mutation rewrites the bytecode and not what a program prints. The ip also describes the mutated layout to whoever reads the output.
evidence: The --levels 0,5,10 sweep fails examples/concurrency/worker_pool.mut: line 18 reads 'vm_runtime_error ip=6 op=OpDiv' at mutation 0 and 'ip=12' at mutation 10. TestRuntimeErrorsIncludeInstructionMetadata requires the metadata, so it is deliberate for errors that end the program.
repro: go run ./cmd/sweep --levels 0,5,10 examples/concurrency/worker_pool.mut
fix_proposal: Decide in Stage B whether script-visible error values carry bytecode positions at all; if not, task_wait (and any builtin that turns a VM error into a value) reports the source position only, and the ip stays in the fatal-error path and debug logs.

title: Twenty-six committed Go files were not gofmt-clean
claim: gofmt, run on the content git stores, flagged 26 files. Most had column alignment one space off, as if formatted on a CRLF copy or by hand. lexer/lexer.go had 119 lines ending in CR CR LF, which also made git treat it as binary. generated_assets.go is written by a generator that never formatted its output, so fixing that file by hand would have been undone by the next asset build.
evidence: The release gate's gofmt step at 07c737a: 26 files not gofmt-clean; the same 26 from gofmt -l over git archive of HEAD with core.autocrlf=false.
repro: git -c core.autocrlf=false archive HEAD -- '*.go' | tar -x -C tmp; gofmt -l tmp
fix_proposal: gofmt the 26 files with the pinned toolchain, keeping each file's line endings; renderReleaseAssetsIndex passes its output through go/format.

title: Two tests assumed a Windows host
claim: TestNormalizeOutput failed on Linux: NormalizeOutput made the slash form of the scratch root with filepath.ToSlash, which leaves a Windows path alone on a host whose separator is already a slash. TestTheCommonRootIsExactAndNeverBareSeparator failed on Linux too: it asserts a drive root (X:\) that only a Windows filepath reads as a volume.
evidence: WSL gate at 07c737a: go test ./... FAIL in mutant/sweep (golden_test.go:65) and mutant/cli (graph_query_test.go:834), 2 of 2 runs.
repro: go test ./sweep/ ./cli/ on Linux at 07c737a.
fix_proposal: Spell the slash rewrite out; skip the drive case where filepath.VolumeName finds no volume.
reporter: Stage A Linux baseline WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: Module parity tests failed on any host the sandbox detector flags
claim: runViaModules compiled through generator.CompileForTest, which injects the debugger and sandbox probes, and ran the result in a secure-mode VM, where a probe that fires ends the run. Under WSL the detector reports a sandbox (type WSL, confidence 100), so ten subtests of TestAnImportAliasNamedAfterABuiltinFamilyIsTheModule and TestAShadowedModuleIsTheSameFileToBothEngines stopped with 'sandbox detected' before resolving anything. The vm package pins its detectors in TestMain for the same reason; these tests could not reach them.
evidence: WSL gate at 07c737a: mutant/parity FAIL, 2 of 2 runs; the other parity tests use plain compiler bytecode and pass.
repro: go test ./parity/ under WSL at 07c737a.
fix_proposal: Run those programs in a VM that is not in secure mode, where a probe that fires warns and the program continues.
reporter: Stage A Linux baseline WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: The sweep reported output that carries the time as a mutation defect
claim: Whether an example is compared across levels was decided by running the first level twice back to back. Output carrying a clock reading or a timer can agree with itself for that long and differ by the next level, and the sweep then failed the example as 'mutation N differs from mutation 0'. Which example failed changed from run to run, so a red gate said nothing about the engine.
evidence: fs_example (a modification time crossing a second) failed 2 of 3 Linux runs; security_quickcheck (a microsecond timer) failed 3 of 3 Windows runs and 1 of 3 Linux runs; both at 07c737a.
repro: Repeat go run ./cmd/sweep --levels 0,5,10 examples/filesystem/fs_example.mut until a run straddles a second.
fix_proposal: Before failing, run both levels again: a mutation defect repeats, output that varies does not.
reporter: Stage A baseline, Windows and WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: Evidence fixtures took their line endings from the checkout
claim: git stores autoruns_hive.json, offline_hive.json and phish.eml in examples/data with LF, and a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf rewrote them to CRLF. fs_integrity_baseline printed their sizes as 1353/847/1471 with one set of SHA-256s on Windows and 1315/814/1431 with another on Linux, so its golden could be right on one host only. It also printed each path with the host's separator.
evidence: WSL sweep at 07c737a: 12 lines of fs_integrity_baseline differ from the Windows-recorded golden; git ls-files --eol showed i/lf w/crlf for the three.
repro: git ls-files --eol examples/data on a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true.
fix_proposal: Mark examples/data/** -text, so a checkout writes the bytes that were committed; print entries by name.
regression_test: go run ./cmd/sweep --golden examples/filesystem/fs_integrity_baseline.mut, on Windows and on Linux
reporter: Stage A Linux baseline WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: On Linux the parent-debugger check matches ordinary words in the parent's arguments
claim: isParentDebugger reads the parent's whole /proc/<ppid>/cmdline, arguments included, lowercases it and substring-matches linuxDebuggerPatterns against it. Short patterns such as 'rr', 'ida' and 'angr' occur inside ordinary words (error, current, concurrency, mirror, validate, candidate), so a parent whose arguments contain one is reported as a debugger. From vm/vm.go:810-822 (read, not run), a secure-mode run would then stop with ErrDebuggerDetected.
evidence: WSL at 07c737a: security_environment_report printed 'debugger detected: false' when the sweep's argv named only that example, and 'true' when it also named examples/concurrency/worker_pool.mut; security_diagnostics_example listed linux:parent_debugger_process.
repro: Under Linux, run a program that calls security_diagnostics() from a parent whose argv contains 'concurrency'.
impact: A Linux user's program can be refused because of the words in the command that started it.
fix_proposal: Compare the parent's executable name (/proc/<ppid>/comm, or argv[0]'s base name) exactly against the list; never search its arguments.
reporter: Stage A Linux baseline WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: The release gate passes on a host that cannot run the race detector
claim: Without gcc the race step reports SKIP, and SKIP does not fail the gate, so a release run on such a host passes with no race coverage at all. The WSL baseline did exactly that.
evidence: WSL gate at 07c737a: 'race detector (test binaries only) SKIP: no gcc; the race detector needs cgo'; the table counted 3 failures, none of them race.
repro: scripts/release_gate.sh --go go1.26.2 on a Linux host without gcc.
fix_proposal: Decide with the owner: either a SKIP of race or sweep fails a full (not --quick) gate, or readiness names the host whose race run it relies on.
reporter: Stage A Linux baseline WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: The shell scripts are committed without the executable bit
claim: Every script under scripts/ is stored as mode 100644, so on a Linux or macOS checkout `scripts/release_gate.sh --go go1.26.2`, the command CONTRIBUTING gives, fails with 'Permission denied' before the gate runs. The same holds for build.sh, coverage.sh and package-vscode-extension.sh. A Windows checkout never shows it: core.filemode is off there.
evidence: git ls-files -s scripts/ lists 100644 for all eight; the Stage A WSL run of the overlaid tree stopped with 'scripts/release_gate.sh: Permission denied' (exit 126).
repro: Clone on Linux and run scripts/release_gate.sh --go go1.26.2.
fix_proposal: The owner runs `git update-index --chmod=+x scripts/build.sh scripts/coverage.sh scripts/package-vscode-extension.sh scripts/release_gate.sh` with the Stage A commit; the file mode is a git change only the owner makes.
reporter: Stage A Linux baseline, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, go1.26.2, 2026-09-24

title: A function value prints its heap address, so a program that ends on one never prints the same thing twice
claim: Closure.Inspect is fmt.Sprintf("Closure[%p]", c), and CompiledFunction and Cell print the same way (object/compiledFnObj.go:81, object/cellObj.go:53). A program whose last value is a function prints a pointer, which differs on every run. examples/modules/lib/stats.mut and report.mut print nothing else, so the sweep can never compare them across levels or give them a golden, and a reader of the output learns an address rather than which function it was.
evidence: go run ./cmd/sweep -v --levels 0,5 examples/modules/lib/stats.mut examples/modules/lib/report.mut printed Closure[0x316fb0af68c0] and Closure[0x3ed91f120b60], and both were classed 'output varies between runs'.
repro: The sweep command in evidence, run twice.
fix_proposal: Print what identifies the function to a reader (its name when bound, its parameter list otherwise), never an address; then give the two module examples goldens.
